thread:
maria: Heads-up — HF->Redwood converter is splitting emoji-containing special tokens. Chat templates that use those tokens break (missing tokens), and quant evals show regressions. Also saw intermittent 403s when fetching safetensors shards which seems to leave a partial file behind. :bug:
kevin: Oof. Which model and how to repro?
maria: model: huggingface.co/ia/emoji-llm v1.2. Repro: `./hf_to_rw convert --model ia/emoji-llm --rev v1.2 --out /tmp/conv` then run `rw-load /tmp/conv` -> generation fails for messages containing the system token `__EMOJI_HELLO__`. Tokenizer.json shows the special token as a single entry, but converted tokenizer splits it. Example: 
```
// original tokenizer.json snippet
"added_tokens": [
  {"id": 50265, "content": "__EMOJI_HELLO__\n😊"}
]
```
After conversion we see tokens like "__EMO", "JI_HELLO__" in the vocab.
ashley: That suggests our converter's special-token handling is doing a naive byte-split or regex that doesn't handle multi-byte emoji sequences. Could be the `special_tokens_regex` escape path.
samir: Also confirming the downloader intermittently returns `HTTP 403` on the last safetensors shard, our downloader does an atomic mv over the temp file but if the file is truncated the subsequent mmap in the runtime will crash/raise. Logs: 
```
GET https://huggingface.co/ia/emoji-llm/resolve/v1.2/weights-00002-of-00004.safetensors 403
WARN downloader: partial file left at /tmp/hub/weights-00002.tmp
OSError: mmap: Invalid argument
```
olga: On top of that, eval numbers: after conversion + 4-bit quant we see a 3-5% drop on our helm prompts. Seems tied to tokenization mismatch for templates containing emoji.
kevin: Can you attach the converted artifact and failing prompts? We need a minimal unit test for CI.
maria: Pushed a small repro bundle to the private hf repo (link: https://huggingface.co/private/ia-emoji-repro, token expires in 24h — DM me). Failing prompt example: `system: Welcome __EMOJI_HELLO__` -> model outputs `Welcome` then stops.
ashley: Quick mitigation: when converting, call `tokenizer.add_tokens([special_token], special_tokens=True)` instead of trying to bake them into the vocab via string split. In Python patch: 
```
# converter fix (draft)
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
# preserve the raw unicode sequence
for s in hf_config.get("special_tokens", []):
    if any(ord(c) > 0xFFFF for c in s):
        tokenizer.add_tokens([s], special_tokens=True)
```
That keeps the emoji as single token and avoids regex/runtime splits.
kevin: Good. Also add a test that roundtrips tokenizer.special_tokens -> saved -> loaded and asserts `encode(special) == [expected_id]`.
deploy-bot: CI: triggered pipeline converters/emoji-fix #1234 by ashley
build-bot: converters/emoji-fix::test_special_token_roundtrip — FAILED (see logs)
ashley: I'm on it, will push a proper patch + fix for the downloader atomic write (write to tmp + fsync + rename) and exponential backoff for 403->retry.
samir: Please also ensure the downloader validates file size / checksum before exposing memmap to runtime. Partial files should be deleted, not renamed.
maria: Thanks — once patch lands I'll re-run the quant eval and post numbers. If that resolves tokenization, we should also re-run the A/B serving test for canary traffic. :eyes:
kevin: Assigning follow-ups: ashley — converter patch + tests; samir — downloader robustness + checksum; maria — repro bundle + eval re-run after patch.
ashley: Ack. Will open PR and link here.
maria: appreciated :thumbsup:
